I run business development for a payments company, and I've learned one hard lesson about conferences. The deals are not lost at the event. They're lost in the three weeks after it. Here's my rule. You have seventy-two hours. In the first three days, people still remember meeting you, and a short message feels natural. After two weeks, the same message feels strange. So on the plane home, I make a simple list: every person, one next step, and a date. Then I send short messages, never long ones. Three lines, one clear question. And if somebody doesn't answer, I don't give up. I try sending something useful instead, like an article or a warm introduction to someone they should meet. That's how a dormant lead comes back to life.

Hi Fabio, it's Priya Nair from Clearline, the fintech from the startup area at Sibos. I hope the trip home was good. I'm calling because I remember talking to you about real-time settlement for trade finance, and I promised to send you our pilot results. They're ready now, and I've just emailed them to you. I also wanted to ask you something. Would it make sense to set up a short call with your innovation team in the next two weeks? I know these things can easily fall through the cracks after a big event, so I thought a quick call might help. Thanks, and talk soon.
